findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource internal ID instead of group ID
findings.body: In `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`, the lambda iterates resources of type "Groups" and calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), …)`, then `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. For V2 per-group resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`, the resource `name` is set to `group.getId()` (via `resolveGroup`), but the resource `id` is the auto-generated primary-key UUID assigned by `ResourceStore.create`. Consequently `findByName(server, groupResource.getId())` never matches the per-group resource, and `hasPermission` silently falls back to the "all-Groups" resource; if the admin has all-Groups scope granted they appear to have view-members/manage-members on every individual group, and the "group IDs" returned in the set are bogus internal UUIDs that the user-provider cannot match. The same logic is used by `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`, `UsersResource.searchForUser` (sets `UserModel.GROUPS`), and `UsersResource.getUsersCount`, so callers will see either empty result sets (because the ID does not match any real group) or count/list inconsistency (`getUsersCount` will return 0 while the search returns users via the post-filter fallback). The fix is to use `groupResource.getName()` (which equals `group.getId()` for per-group resources) and pass it into both `hasPermission` and the resulting `granted` set; additionally the all-Groups sentinel resource (where `getName()` equals the type string `Groups`) must be skipped, since it is not a real group ID. Mirroring the V1 implementation, which correctly uses `resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`, would resolve this.

findings.title: Possible NPE in hasPermission when type resource is null
findings.body: `hasPermission` assigns `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE);` and immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty();` without a null check. `getResourceTypeResource` can legitimately return null (when FGAP V2 is enabled but the "Groups" schema resource has not yet been created in the authz resource store, or when `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false, etc.). The JPA `PolicyStore.findByResource` implementation dereferences `resource.getId()`, so calling it with a null `Resource` argument will throw a NullPointerException at runtime. The same pattern exists in `UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission` at the `findByResource(server, resource)` call. Add an explicit null guard before invoking `findByResource` (e.g., `if (resource == null || policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) return false;`).

findings.title: Possible NPE in hasPermission when type resource is null
findings.body: Same defect as in `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission`: after falling back to the all-Users schema resource via `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, the code calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` without checking whether `getResourceTypeResource` returned null. The JPA `PolicyStore.findByResource` dereferences `resource.getId()` and will throw a NullPointerException for a null resource. Guard the call with a null check (e.g., `if (resource == null || policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) return false;`).

findings.title: Javadoc on canManageMembership contradicts V2 semantics
findings.body: The interface Javadoc for `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` says it returns true if the caller has `MANAGE_USERS` "Or if it has a permission to `MANAGE` the group or `MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP` of the group." However `GroupPermissionsV2.canManageMembership` actually also delegates to `hasPermission(..., MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP)`, which corresponds to the documented behaviour (MANAGE or MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP). The V1 implementation, by contrast, accepts MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP only (via `hasPermission(group, MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP_SCOPE)`) and treats a `canManage(group)` match (which itself requires MANAGE on the specific group, not just MANAGE on all-groups) as a shortcut. The single Javadoc comment cannot describe both contracts accurately. Either split the behaviour or document that the V2 implementation effectively treats `MANAGE` of the group (anywhere) as sufficient to manage membership of that group, which is a broader grant than V1.

findings.title: Javadoc on canViewMembers contradicts V2 semantics
findings.body: The Javadoc for `canViewMembers(GroupModel)` describes the V1 contract (which was just `VIEW_MEMBERS`). Both the V1 (post-PR) and V2 implementations additionally accept `MANAGE_MEMBERS`. Either the comment should be updated to mention `MANAGE_MEMBERS` as well, or the implementations should only accept `VIEW_MEMBERS`. Note that accepting `MANAGE_MEMBERS` is a behaviour change relative to what the V1 implementation did before this PR (it used to return `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` only), and the Javadoc does not warn administrators that a `manage-members` grant now implicitly grants view-members.
